Technology stocks still were firming Tuesday afternoon, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding over 0.4% in value, retreating from a more than 1% increase earlier in the session, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was climbing just under 0.8%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Link Motion ( LKM ) still was nearly 1% higher Tuesday afternoon, drifting off a nearly 9% spike soon after the opening bell that followed the Chinese "smart" car company announcing a new strategic partnership with Alibaba's ( BABA ) AutoNavi digital-mapping unit. Under terms of the partnership agreement, AutoNavi will guide riders directly from its popular mapping application to Link Motion's smart ride service in all of Link Motion's current markets. Link Motion also will use AutoNavi's mapping and navigation applications in its "smart" ride business.
In other sector news:
+ Alphabet (GOOG,GOOGL) climbed to a record high on Tuesday, rising over 5% to a best-ever $1266 a share, after the technology conglomerate reported Q2 operating income and revenue, prompting several analyst to increase their price targets for the company's stock. Excluding a $5 billion anti-trust fine by the European Union the company plans to appeal, Google earned $11.75 per share, up from $8.90 per share last year and exceeding the Street view expecting $9.54 per share. GAAP earnings fell to $4.54 per share from $5.01 per share during the same quarter last year but still also topped the $3.58 a share Capital IQ consensus. Revenue grew to $32.7 billion from $26 billion last year, also surpassing the $32.1 billion Street view.
Following the better-than-expected results, Canaccord raised its price target by $20 to $1,170 a share based on 24 times its projected FY19 earnings of $48.75 per share. Also, Oppenheimer reiterates its Outperform investment rating for Alphabet and increased its price target for the company's stock by $100 to $1,450, while Stifel Nicolaus boosted its price target by $222 to $1,456 a share and kept its Buy rating. Also Tuesday, Canaccord Genuity lifted its price target by $120 to $1,170 a share.
